messages:
miguel: heads-up — after the envoy egress policy rollout in eu-west1 a bunch of model pods started failing readiness/healthchecks. failing outbound calls to the metadata IP and our internal registry.

deploy-bot: Rollout complete: envoy-egress-policy v3 deployed to eu-west1 (2026-03-12T08:40:00Z)

lexi: seeing the same in logs — envoy: "upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers" for a lot of requests. any quick rollback option?

miguel: repro steps i used: 

```
# inside an impacted pod
kubectl exec -it pod/model-xyz -- curl -v http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/
* Rebuilt URL to: http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/
*   Trying 169.254.169.254...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* connect to 169.254.169.254 port 80 failed: Connection reset by peer
* Failed to connect to 169.254.169.254 port 80: Connection reset by peer
* Closing connection 0
curl: (7) Failed to connect to 169.254.169.254 port 80: Connection reset by peer
```

miguel: similar for internal-artifact-registry.redwood.svc:443 -> immediate resets. healthcheck endpoints hit these upstreams during startup so pods never become ready.

sam: that error usually means the sidecar is intercepting the traffic and actively rejecting it. Did the new policy flip to deny-by-default and drop some important CIDRs (169.254.169.254, 10.12.0.0/16)?

anya: checking the egress-gateway config now — i can see the new filter chain. there is a route matching 0.0.0.0/0 with an http filter that strips CONNECT and enforces L7. metadata and our registry expect raw TCP or CONNECT passthrough. looks like strip_connect: true got enabled accidentally.

lexi: oh, that would break both metadata and docker/registry pulls. also noticed the allowlist CIDR in the rollout was `10.12/16` (no netmask) — config parser treated it as a single host so the whole subnet got blocked.

ops-oncall: mitigation options: 
1) hotfix the egress policy to explicitly allow 169.254.169.254/32 and registry CIDRs with passthrough/tcp-proxy rules, then roll forward.
2) or rollback envoy-egress-policy to v2 in eu-west1 to restore previous behavior.

sam: +1 to explicit allowlist hotfix if we can push quickly. but rollback is safest if hotfix risks more traffic gaps.

miguel: i'm starting a rollback now to buy time, and anya will prepare the allowlist PR in parallel.

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated: envoy-egress-policy -> v2 for eu-west1 by miguel.

anya: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/infrastructure/pull/789 — adds explicit egress rules: 169.254.169.254/32 passthrough, 10.12.0.0/16 allow tcp CONNECT, and registry FQDN -> pinned IP ranges. requests reviewers: sam, lexi.

sam: confirmed — after rollback healthchecks for ~12/15 impacted pods turned green within 90s. remaining pods are restarting and pulling artifacts successfully now. monitoring for 10m. :thumbsup:

miguel: thanks all. postmortem notes: default-deny egress policies must include a metadata passthrough and we need unit tests that simulate metadata+registry pulls during rollout. creating follow-up ticket.

ops-oncall: creating incident ticket INC-2026-218 and tagging eng-infra + eng-runtime for coordination.
